steps.content:
█Number: FAC-M-136-I
█File: Sinner's Arrest Report

A Sinner was arrested by the MBCC Arrest Unit in the latest locale where the myth of Mad Shears appeared. The arrestee was barely conscious at the time of arrest and is presumed to be Adela, an S-Class Sinner at large.
Adela is a suspect in a series of attacks on Sloane Street. Although no video evidence is available, it's believed that she's capable of mental interference. She's extremely dangerous and must be detained immediately.

*Annex—Performance in Serving Term (PERF):
The Sinner has been detained. An interrogation by the MBCC chief is urgently needed. Furthermore, MBCC supervision of the Sinner should be strengthened to keep her dangerous behavior in check.
You walk into the interrogation room. Seated at the table is Adela the Sinner. She looks up at you with a smile on her face.
She looks harmless, with her gentle smile and slight build. Appearances can be deceptive, however. You know how dangerous she is.
You put the PERF report and evidence bag on the table and sit down across from Adela. You notice that she's looking at your face with interest.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Oh, nothing. It's just that you look familiar.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I have a feeling that I've seen you before, but I can't place you. Have we met before?
You don't remember meeting Adela.
I guess this is our first meeting, Miss Mad Shears.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I was mistaken, then. Sorry!
You don't remember meeting Adela, but...
I'm not sure. Maybe we met on Sloane Street, where I was attacked by a mysterious being and lost the memories of that day. Have you been to Sloane Street, Miss Mad Shears?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Sloane Street? Yet another place I've never heard of.
Adela remains calm, unruffled by your accusatory tone. But she didn't contradict you when you called her Miss Mad Shears.
You're dealing with a seemingly cool-headed individual with a streak of madness.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You must have brought me here for a reason. Why don't you tell me how I can be of help, Chief?
You have so many questions about the Fog Alley attacks and Mad Shears herself.

None of the Fog Alley attacks was captured on film, and the victims and other people who had been on the scene, affected by the Sinner's power, couldn't remember what he or she looked like. The only thing the Arrest Unit had to go by was the reported sightings of Mad Shears. Despite the lack of information, they were able to apprehend Adela, who was losing control of her power at the time of arrest.
But you have a more urgent matter to deal with at the moment.
In a matter of days, S-Class Sinner Adela attacked eleven people, including MBCC staffers and Sinners. Ten of them have suffered mental impairment to various degrees.

steps.speaker: Narration
steps.content: You glance at Adela out of the corner of your eye. She's still wearing that gentle smile of hers. You have a hard time reconciling the harmless-looking woman in front of you with Mad Shears in the urban myth, or with the dangerous Sinner in the PERF report.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You don't look well. They're important to you, aren't they? And you're worried about their well-being?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You don't have to worry. They're not in any danger. They'll sleep it off, and when they wake up, they'll be as good as new.

options: Their well-being is none of your concern.
I'm not here to talk about them.

choices.text: Their well-being is none of your concern.
I'm not here to talk about them.

steps.content: Here in the MBCC, everyone understands what they've signed up for. I've done everything in my power to protect them against Mania, and they're forever ready to face it when it's necessary.
What I want to know is why you attacked them.
I know you didn't do it to break out.

Many of the detained Sinners have tried to break out of the MBCC, but Adela hasn't been one of them. She didn't run away after her attacks. Instead, she sent the victims to the lounge area and stayed on the premises.
Why did you do it then?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Why? I was just trying to help them.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Their hair was too long. They carried it everywhere they went. It weighed them down.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It upset me to see them like that. So I cut the troublesome hair off to make them feel more comfortable. I didn't mean to cause any trouble. I'm sorry about that.
Adela sighs. She sounds sincere, even though her explanation is absurd.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Oh sorry, I forgot to explain it to you.
She brushes a stray lock of hair from her eyes, her smile never fading.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Your hair grows rapidly if you carry a lot of worries in your mind. The more worries you carry, the longer the hair.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I was just trying to help them get rid of their worries.
I have no idea what you're talking about.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Maybe only those who hold the shears can see the rapidly growing hair, but...
Her gaze is still on you, but her smile is gone.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I did make some mistakes in the past and got some people in trouble. But I won't make the same mistakes again.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I want to trim away other people's worries. It's always been my responsibility, and mine alone.
You don't fully understand what she's saying, but you've taken notice of a useful piece of information in her gibberish.
You said you want to trim away other people's worries?
Was that why you attacked those Sloane Street residents trapped in thick fog? To trim away their worries?

options: Produce the report on the Sloane Street attacks

choices.text: Produce the report on the Sloane Street attacks

steps.content: It's discovered that all the Sloane Street victims suffered from memory loss, as have the MBCC staffers who you attacked.
Are you still claiming you're innocent?
You look into her eyes, trying to see if they betray anything.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I have no idea what you're talking about. I don't remember going to Sloane Street. I don't know anything about that place.
You've interrogated many Sinners. You know a liar when you see one. The eyes of the woman in front of you betray nothing; she seems very genuine.
Maybe she is a highly accomplished liar? Or maybe she's successfully trained herself to remain calm in whatever situation?
You can't decide which. You need more clues.

You have Adela's suitcase brought into the interrogation room. It's an important piece of physical evidence collected at the time of her arrest.
The lock on this exquisite suitcase is intact. When Adela notices how it's not been forced open, she gives you a compliment, still wearing her trademark smile.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You're quite the gentleman.
I don't deserve such a compliment. I didn't open it, not because I didn't want to, but because I didn't get around to it.
Mind if I open it, Miss Adela?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Do I get to say no?
Still smiling, Adela gives a small wave of her hand.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Be my guest.
When you open it, you're greeted by a faint scent of lavender. Everything inside is neatly organized: clothes, toiletries, papers. The owner must be a very organized lady, you think to yourself.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: As you can see, nothing out of the ordinary...
The papers catch your attention. They might bear some useful information.

options: Take the papers out of the suitcase

choices.text: Take the papers out of the suitcase

steps.content: A business license for a hair salon in Ashby Village, receipts for furniture purchased in the Central Business District, a lease on an apartment on Sloane Street...
These papers—some old, some new, have been tucked away in one of the compartments.
Do you have anything to say about this?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You mean the papers? I have this old habit of saving receipts and stuff. They might come in handy. That's what I thought anyway.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Now I realize I might be wrong. They take up space in my suitcase, and I haven't found a use for them yet. I've never got around to throwing them away. Now I have a big pile of them.

options: I'm not asking about your habit.

choices.text: I'm not asking about your habit.

steps.content: Ashby Village, the Central Business District, Sloane Street, which I mentioned just now...
Do you know what these places have in common? The answer is the myth of Mad Shears.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Really? I didn't know that.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: None of the names you just mentioned rings a bell.
Don't play me for a fool. Your power is unique. No other Sinner in all of DisCity can do what you do.

Adela looks unperturbed. You've met your share of accomplished liars in the past, and you've always been able to spot a crack or two in their veneer. The same can't be said of the woman in front of you.
Or maybe she is telling the truth. If that's the case, then the only possible explanation...

options: Did you erase your own memories?

choices.text: Did you erase your own memories?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: We all have troublesome memories. I'm no exception.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Maybe I did go to those places. Maybe I did erase those people's troublesome memories, and mine as well. Either way, I have no recollection of any of it.
Adela remains unperturbed—disturbingly so, for some reason.
It makes no sense. Why would you do that to yourself?
A faint smile crosses her lips. And then she starts explaining.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Whenever I get the chance, I listen to my beloved customers' troubles and remove those troubles for them afterward, so that they can carry on with their lives worry-free. That's my calling.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: After I free them of their unpleasant memories, including the memories of me, I do the same to myself.

options: What do you gain from all this?

choices.text: What do you gain from all this?

steps.content: Adela closes her eyes. She opens them moments later and answers your question.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Inner peace.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I gain inner peace. I'm free of worries.
It's ridiculous.
Are you telling me that every time you experience something unpleasant, your solution, your only solution, is to erase the memory connected with that experience?
You're getting worked up. Adela doesn't react strongly. She leans forward ever slightly, a concerned look on her face.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You look upset. Did I cause it?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Do you need my help?
Her words of concern send a chill down your spine. The fire of anger that was burning inside you just a moment ago has been instantly doused.
You blurt out your refusal.
I don't need your help. I don't want to have my "unpleasant" memories erased.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Are you sure?
She smiles, somewhat ruefully.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: What a shame.
The brief exchange gets your adrenalin pumping. You can feel the shackles vibrating inside you.
Fortunately, Adela doesn't make further moves to escalate the situation. Now there's a brief silence.

You take a moment to calm yourself down. You now realize that your line of questioning is getting you nowhere. How do you expect to extract any useful information from someone who erases their own memories?

options: Go through the contents of the suitcase for other clues

choices.text: Go through the contents of the suitcase for other clues

steps.content: As you go through the contents of the suitcase, Adela looks at you with a ghost of a smile on her face. Both of you remain silent.
You find a bunch of keys in a hidden compartment.
The keys are covered with rust. There's a tag attached to the key ring. On it are a few vaguely identifiable words.
12 Dorset Street, Apt. E.
Do you remember this place?
You've asked the question in a somewhat offhand manner, only expecting "I don't remember" or "It doesn't ring a bell" as an answer from her.
Your interest is piqued when Adela doesn't answer you right away. You look up and see her expression has changed slightly.
But it only lasts a second. And then she delivers what's become something of a catchphrase for her.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Doesn't ring a bell. Sorry.
Why did she hesitate? Why does she keep the keys? The address must hold great significance for her, you think as you run your finger over the piece of paper, which has grown soft with age.
These are the only keys in your suitcase. They're rusty, but you didn't get rid of them. They must mean something to you.
Dorset Street is where the myth of Mad Shears originated. Maybe that's where you lived before you became Mad Shears.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: What does it matter where I lived before I became Mad Shears?
I don't know yet. It's worth checking out, don't you think? As part of the investigation.
I hope you can accompany me on this trip. Your participation is essential.
Adela shakes her head, her smile now tinged with resignation.
